correctness.rationale: For all N≥3, unitary three-column Gram algebra proves the three-node branch. A four-node signed rule at gcd(N,6)=1 would force e2(z1,z2,z3,z4)=0, a six-root vanishing sum prohibited by Lam–Leung Theorem 5.2. An explicit positive four-node rule covers every even order not divisible by three, and Carathéodory in R4 proves the five-node upper bound in the remaining case. Lagrange interpolation yields the exact unique feasible weights on any five nodes. The included checker independently corroborated 77 orders and 202467 four-node tests; finite tests are not the proof.

value.rationale: For the smallest consecutive cyclic support requiring two independent Fourier cancellations, this is the exact minimal positive sampling budget at every order. It explains arithmetic phase transitions at divisibility by 2 and 3, gives explicit constructive and uniqueness criteria, and demonstrates an unbounded prime-order sample saving versus equal weights (p to 5), with a genuine application to finite Parseval Fourier design.
